text:
kai: Quick sanity check — after switching the q8 7B model to FlashAttention v3 on H100 L40 we see mean p50 down ~18% but p95 spikes in eu-central. Uploading the small bench output.

morgan: Can you paste the numbers? region, seq_len, batch, p50/p95, oom counts?

kai: sure — from the short sweep (single node, 1 stream each):

```
region      seq  batch  kernel      p50_ms  p95_ms  qps
us-west     1024 4      triton       32      95     280
us-west     1024 4      flashv3      26      110    340
eu-central  1024 4      triton       35      120    260
eu-central  1024 4      flashv3      28      170    360  <-- big tail
ap-south    2048 2      triton       60      200    90
ap-south    2048 2      flashv3      50      240    110
```
No OOMs in this quick run, but p95 variance is real in eu.

nina: interesting. echoing past notes — flashv3 gains on throughput and median but can expose tail variance due to kernel-path choices + allocator fragmentation for longer seqs. Triton tends to be more stable p95 but lower peak qps.

sam: also worth checking driver + CUDA versions. our eu images were on 535.x stack; us-west on 540.x. vendor libs (cuDNN/CUTLASS tweaks) can shift kernels. did you pin drivers?

kai: good catch — we didn’t. eu still on 535. i'll repro with 540. also running a memcheck to see fragmentation.

alex: operationally we should codify a simple kernel-selection heuristic and hysteresis:
- prefer flashv3 when seq <= 2048 and p50 improvement > 12% AND p95 delta < 40% relative
- prefer triton when seq > 2048 or when p95_regression_count > 3 in 1h
- add a 30m cooldown after switching to avoid flip-flops

nina: +1. add region check: if region has older driver or less NVLink bandwidth, weight towards Triton. and make fallback automatic if p95 > 150ms for two consecutive 5m windows.

morgan: what about vendor kernels (cuDNN/CUBLAS config)? In some private clusters we've seen vendor libs best for short-context chat (seq<512) with tiny batches.

kai: yes — for seq <512 and batch <=2, cuDNN fused kernels beat both in median latency. tradeoff: limited sequence support and tricky tuning params.

bench-bot: bench upload: https://bench.redwood/internal/1829/flashv3-vs-triton-quick-sweep — includes raw traces and per-request lat histogram.

sam: plan for next steps:
- kai: repro with unified driver 540 in eu + memprof capture (2h run)
- nina: produce candidate heuristic PR for runtime routing + tests
- alex: add canary route in console with automated fallback to triton and a 30m cooldown
- morgan: run vendor-kernel quick sweep on private cluster for seq 256/512

kai: will run now. ping if you want to join the run. :thumbsup:

alex: nice — once we have 2-region 2h runs we'll set rollout rules. also add an eval check for model quality (sampling) to ensure quant changes + kernel dont change outputs.

morgan: thanks all. small note — if flashv3 improves qps by >20% we might accept a moderate p95 hit for background batch jobs but not for sync chat routes.

kai: noted. starting the runs, will post updates in this thread.
